sections.h2: What are the options for a quick Perinton sale?
sections.html:
A Perinton owner can list, sell privately or take a direct cash offer, and a cash route is worth pricing if the house needs work or the owner needs to close soon. The town just finished a townwide revaluation, so a new assessment sits on every parcel and buyers will read it closely.

Perinton is in eastern Monroe County about 10 miles southeast of Rochester. Local paperwork runs through the town's Assessment Office and Building and Codes Department, both at Town Hall on Turk Hill Road, and deeds are recorded by the Monroe County Clerk in Rochester.

sections.h2: What is Perinton and how did it grow?
sections.html:
The town was established in 1812 and covers 34.56 square miles. Its neighbors are East Rochester, Victor, Macedon, Pittsford and Penfield, and its southern line is the Ontario County border. The Village of Fairport sits inside the town on the Erie Canal, and the hamlets include Egypt in the east and Bushnell's Basin in the southwest, where Richardson's Canal House has been on the National Register of Historic Places since 1980.

Settlement began in 1793, when Glover Perrin and his family arrived. Canal and railroad access made Fairport an industrial port from the 1850s, home to firms such as the American Can Company. Outside the village the town stayed rural until the 1950s, and suburban subdivisions now surround the remaining farms. Perinton calls itself a Trail Town USA and maintains the 35-mile Crescent Trail, along with Egypt Park, Perinton Park, Powder Mills Park and Garnsey Arboretum.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Perinton homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 47,479 people in 2020 and estimates 46,823 for July 1, 2025, a change of negative 1.4 percent. The 2020 to 2024 survey gives these housing facts:

  • Owner-occupied rate: 79.2 percent.
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $310,200.
  • Median gross rent: $1,349.
  • Median household income: $112,093, across 20,347 households.
  • Residents 65 or older: 23.8 percent.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher: 62.8 percent.

Nearly a quarter of residents are 65 or older, so a good share of Perinton sales come from retirees who are moving, downsizing or settling an estate. Those sellers often value a firm closing date over the highest possible price.

sections.h2: What changed in the 2026 Perinton revaluation?
sections.html:
The town updated every assessment because the last full update came in 2018 and its equalization rate had slid from 100 percent to 57 percent. The Assessment Office says a revaluation does not raise the total tax collected. It changes how the same levy is divided, and the new values first show up on the 2026 to 2027 tax bills.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Perinton assessment?
sections.html:
Taxes cannot be grieved, but the assessment can. Grievance Day for the next cycle is Tuesday, May 25, 2027, and applications are accepted from May 1 until 8:00 p.m. that day. A mailed form must arrive by the deadline regardless of its postmark.

  • File New York form RP-524, with all four pages completed and signed.
  • Send the original and five copies of the form and the supporting papers.
  • Attach evidence: a closing statement, a listing history, comparable sales, an appraisal or construction costs.
  • Income property needs at least three years of income and expense data.

You do not have to appear in person. Decisions are mailed on or before July 1. After that, the final roll sets the school tax bill for September 1, the town and county bill for January 1 and any village bill for June 1.

sections.h2: What should a Perinton seller review before listing?
sections.html:
The assessment cycle gives a rough timeline. The Assessment Office inspects new construction, remodeling and demolitions from July 1 through March 1, and informal reviews open each October 1. The tentative roll is filed May 1 and the final roll July 1, so a sale in late spring happens while next year's number is still being argued.

  • Read your preliminary assessment notice and compare it with recent sales on the town's sales file.
  • Confirm that every deck, finished basement or addition has a closed permit.
  • Note whether the house is in Fairport village, since a village bill may apply.
  • Gather the deed, payoff statements and your exemption paperwork.

Once those are set, a listing, a private sale and a cash offer can be weighed on the same facts.

Town-administered exemption applications are due March 1. The Assessment Office names these:

  • Senior Citizen.
  • Persons with Disabilities and Limited Income.
  • Veterans.
  • Volunteer Firefighter or Volunteer Ambulance Worker.
  • STAR, which the State administers at tax.ny.gov/star or (518) 457-2036.

Seniors who already hold an exemption are mailed a renewal from June 2026 through January 2027, and each renewal sets an intake appointment. Questions go to the Assessment Office at (585) 223-0770. A buyer should plan to file after closing.

sections.h2: What do Perinton's Building and Codes rules mean for a sale?
sections.html:
Perinton says that work done without a required permit can hold up the sale of a property and can affect an insurance claim. It also warns that the town can issue stop work or cease and desist orders until a permit is obtained. Permits are needed for decks, porches, three-season rooms, finished basements, garages, sheds, fireplaces, generators, fences, hot tubs and pools that hold 24 inches of water or more.

Re-roofing, re-siding, flooring, cabinet installation and replacing windows or doors without enlarging openings usually do not need one. A final inspection leads to a Certificate of Compliance or Occupancy, and the space cannot be used until one is issued. A home business needs both a building permit and a Certificate of Occupancy before it starts. Ask the Building and Codes Department for your address history before listing.

sections.h2: Who covers police, fire and taxes inside Perinton?
sections.html:
The Monroe County Sheriff provides primary law enforcement, and the Village of Fairport has its own police department. Four volunteer fire protection districts split the town: Bushnell's Basin, Egypt, Forest Hills and Perinton. A house inside the village can also carry a village tax bill, so ask where the parcel sits.

Delinquent taxes lead to Monroe County's in rem foreclosure. Action No. 150 covers parcels in Perinton, including the Village of Fairport, and set a public auction for September 11, 2026, a date that has passed. County recording of a deed costs $50 for the first page, and the state taxes the transfer at $2 per $500.

faqs.q: Did Perinton reassess every home recently?
faqs.a: Yes. The town completed a townwide revaluation in 2026, the first since 2018. The Assessment Office mailed 18,234 preliminary notices in March 2026 and says the new values appear on the 2026 to 2027 tax bills.

faqs.q: When is the next Perinton Grievance Day?
faqs.a: May 25, 2027, with filing open from May 1 and a final deadline of 8:00 p.m. that evening. Late or postmark-only mailings will not be reviewed.

faqs.q: Does a revaluation raise my taxes?
faqs.a: Not by itself. The Assessment Office explains that the town's tax levy is set through budgets, so a new assessment only changes how that total is shared. Your bill can rise, fall or stay level depending on how your value compares with others.

faqs.q: Is Fairport the same as Perinton?
faqs.a: No. The Village of Fairport is one part of the town of Perinton, located on the Erie Canal in the northwestern portion. A village tax bill may apply to parcels inside the village.

faqs.q: Can unpermitted work stop a Perinton sale?
faqs.a: It can. The town says work done without a required permit may hold up a sale and complicate insurance claims, and a space cannot be occupied until the Building and Codes Department issues a Certificate of Compliance or Occupancy.
